subject.title: [security] Azure disk cleanup can authorize deletion from stale adopted ownership tags

question: Should Azure owned cleanup require `disk.managedBy` to match the releasing VM for every managed disk deletion, including already-tagged disks and retries after the VM has disappeared?
rationale: The live-VM race fix is narrow, but current tests preserve cleanup of tagged companion resources after VM deletion, so maintainers need to choose the acceptable orphaned-disk boundary for a destructive security-sensitive action.

options.title: Require fresh association
options.body: Fail closed unless the disk currently reports `managedBy` for the releasing VM, and add regression coverage for tagged and untagged disk paths.

options.title: Add orphaned-disk claim
options.body: Permit post-VM disk cleanup only through an equally strong lease-bound claim that stale tag adoption cannot create by itself.

options.title: Accept tag-based cleanup
options.body: Keep the current retry behavior and document that adopted Azure disk tags are sufficient ownership proof once Crabbox writes them.

recommendation.title: Require fresh association
recommendation.body: Fail closed unless the disk currently reports `managedBy` for the releasing VM, and add regression coverage for tagged and untagged disk paths.

likelyOwner.reason: He authored the recent Azure provider-ownership hardening path and its tests, including the current disk adoption behavior.
